analysis:
Reviewed the docs-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch adds one failure-mode table row at head line 2371. It documents that a cold load can be refused with a 503 or an insufficient-memory error while an idle model is resident, because an unexpired Autopilot placement hold excludes that slot from eviction and gives its weights no reclaim credit. The two supplied units (head lines 1228-2037) are unchanged surrounding documentation, and the added row sits outside those excerpts. I examined the surrounding text on prefix cache, MTP, deadlines, sampling, tool parsing and media caps and found nothing that alters a control.

Security relevance: the row describes an availability behavior, where a hold can delay another model's load. That is related to DoS-class threats on the TB-007 and TB-002 boundaries, such as T-029, because a held slot can keep memory occupied. The hold is a documented, expiring, provider-local scheduling policy. I cannot see how a consumer or provider could trigger or extend a hold, so there is no evidence of a new attack surface or a regression. The code path (ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift: autopilotHoldsModel, autopilotHeldWeightBytes, evictableModelSlots) was not supplied, so I could not verify that the documented behavior matches the code, or that hold expiry is bounded and authenticated.

The T-041 cache details (30-minute TTL, HMAC names, default-on SSD tier) are unchanged here. Nothing in the visible text loosens the TTL, scope derivation or encryption. No threat-model update is indicated by this documentation line. Remaining question for integration: confirm in the Autopilot code that placement holds are coordinator- or operator-authored, expire, and cannot be abused by a consumer to starve model loads.
